**Finding: compliant** — no redline proposed.

The Article II grant meets the preferred position on every material term of the LICENSE rule:

- **Affiliates:** §2.2(a) gives Ono the right to sublicense the Array Patents and Know-How to its Affiliates without Array consent (consent is required only for Third Party sublicensees/distributors).
- **Contractors:** §2.1(b) expressly allows the manufacturing licence to be "extended by Ono to Third Party manufacturers for Manufacturing the Products on Ono's behalf," and the §1.57 "Subcontractor" definition contemplates a Party or its Affiliate subcontracting performance of any activities under the Agreement.
- **Not revocable at will:** Array's only termination rights are uncured material breach (§13.3, 90/60-day cure) and insolvency (§13.4). There is no at-will termination in Array's favour, and §13.1 converts the licences on expiry into "fully paid-up, irrevocable, perpetual, royalty free licenses, with sublicensing rights."
- **Successor transfer:** §18.9 permits assignment without the other Party's consent to an entity acquiring substantially all of the business or assets, whether by merger or acquisition.

Noted but not flagged: Array's prior written consent for Third Party sublicensees and distributors is not qualified by a reasonableness standard — a customary limitation in a territory licence of this type and a sub-element only, so it is recorded in the rationale rather than redlined.
